  • Traction battery

    1. Scope of application

The regulation specifies the test method concerning the high voltage traction battery (excluding traction batteries for mild hybrids 60 V and under) used for motor vehicles (except two-wheeled motor vehicles) to confirm safety in the physical, chemical, electrical and thermal impact conditions. It applies to the traction battery pursuant to Article 18-3 of KMVSS.

    1. Definitions

  • 2.1 “High Voltage” means the classification of an electric component or circuit, if its working

voltage is > 60 V and ≤ 1500 V DC or > 30 V and ≤ 1000 V AC root mean square (rms).

  • 2.2 “Fire” means the emission of flames from a Tested-Device. Sparks and arcing shall not be

considered as flames.

  • 2.3 “Venting” means the release of excessive internal pressure from cell or battery in a manner

intended by design to preclude rupture or explosion.

  • 2.4 “Attached equipment” means the equipment installed additionally for the function and

safety of a REESS such as BMS, safety device, and cooling device, etc.

  • 2.5 “Cell” means a single encased electrochemical unit containing one positive and one

negative terminal, which exhibits a voltage differential across its two terminals.

  • 2.6 “Tested-Device” means either the complete REESS or REESS subsystem that is subjected

to the tests prescribed by this Regulation.

  • 2.7 “Safety device” means a device, such as fuse, diode, current breaker etc. which cuts

off the current upon abnormal operation of the traction battery.

  • 2.8 “Enclosure” means the part enclosing the internal units and providing protection against

direct contact.

  • 2.9. “Electrolyte leakage” means the escape of electrolyte from the Rechargeable Electrical

Energy Storage System (REESS) in the form of liquid.

  • 2.10 “Rupture” means opening(s) through the casing of any functional cell assembly created

or enlarged by an event, large enough for a 12 mm diameter test finger (IPXXB) to penetrate and make contact with live parts.

  • 2.11 “Explosion” means the sudden release of energy sufficient to cause pressure waves

and/or projectiles that may cause structural and/or physical damage to the surrounding of the Tested-Device.

  • 2.12 “BMS (Battery Management System)” means a system controlling the function of

the REESS by measuring the current, voltage, and temperature etc. to control the charging or discharging current for efficient usage of the REESS, and operating the safety device upon abnormal operation.

  • 2.13 “State of Charge (SOC)” means the available electrical charge in a Tested-Device

expressed as a percentage of its rated capacity.

  • 2.14 “Mild hybrid” refers to a method in which a vehicle partially uses an electric motor to

assist the engine only during starting and low-speed driving.

    1. Test conditions

  • 5.1. Procedure for conducting a standard cycle of charge/discharge

Det. Reg. of KMVSS-MOLIT Notification No. 2021-694 MOLIT Notification 2023-7 5
Traction battery 2021.05.10 2023.01.02

©KAIDA

  • 5.1.1 A standard cycle shall start with a standard discharge and is followed by a standard

charge. The standard cycle of charge/discharge shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 293 K ± 10 K (20 ± 10 °C). The standard charge/discharge procedure including termination criteria shall be defined by the manufacturer.

  • 5.1.2 If not specified, then it shall be a discharge with 1C (quantity of electric charge,

Coulomb) current. For a complete vehicle going through the discharge procedure using a dynamometer, discharge termination will be according to vehicle controls. Rest period after discharge shall be minimum 15 min.

  • 5.1.3 If the charge procedure is not defined by the manufacturer, then it shall be a charge with

C/3 current. Charging is continued until normally terminated. Charge condition shall be according to paragraph 48.5.2.2 for a complete REESS or REESS subsystem.

  • 5.1.4 For a complete vehicle that can be charged by an external source or by a dynamometer,

charge termination shall be according to vehicle controls.

  • 5.2 Procedures for SOC adjustment.

  • 5.2.1 The adjustment of SOC shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 293 K ± 10 K

(20 ± 10 °C) for vehicle-based tests and 295 K ± 5 K (22 ± 5 °C) for component-based tests.

  • 5.2.2 The SOC of the Tested-Device shall be adjusted in accordance with one of the following

procedures as applicable. Where different charging procedures are possible, the REESS shall be charged using the procedure which yields the highest SOC:

  • 5.2.2.1 For a vehicle with a REESS designed to be externally charged, the REESS shall be

charged to the highest SOC in accordance with the procedure specified by the manufacturer.

  • 5.2.2.2 For a vehicle with a REESS designed to be charged only by an energy source on the

vehicle, the REESS shall be charged to the highest SOC which is achievable with normal operation of the vehicle. The manufacturer shall advise on the vehicle operation mode to achieve this SOC.

  • 5.2.2.3 In case that the complete REESS or REESS sub-system is used as the Tested-Device,

the Tested-Device shall be charged to the highest SOC in accordance with the procedure specified by the manufacturer. Procedures specified by the manufacturer for manufacturing, service or maintenance may be considered as appropriate if they achieve an equivalent SOC as for that under normal operating conditions. In case the Tested-Device does not control SOC by itself, the SOC shall be charged to not less than 95 per cent of the maximum normal operating SOC.

  • 5.2.3 When the complete REESS or REESS subsystem is tested, the SOC shall be no less than

95 per cent of the SOC for REESS designed to be externally charged and shall be no less than 90 per cent of SOC for REESS designed to be charged only by an energy source on the vehicle according to paragraphs 48.5.2.1 and 48.5.2.2. The SOC will be confirmed by a method provided by the manufacturer.

  • 7 Test procedures for PC and bus/truck/special purpose vehicle with a GVW of 4.5 tons or less

  • 7.1 Vibration test.

  • 7.1.1 Purpose

The purpose of this test is to verify the safety performance of the REESS under a vibration environment which the REESS will likely experience during the normal operation of the vehicle.

  • 7.1.2 Installations

  • 7.1.2.1 This test shall be conducted either with the complete REESS or with REESS

subsystem(s). If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s), the test result shall represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions. If the electronic management control unit for the REESS is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells, then the electronic management unit may be omitted from installation on the Tested-Device if so requested by the manufacturer.

  • 7.1.2.2 The Tested-Device shall be firmly secured to the platform of the vibration machine in

such a manner as to ensure that the vibrations are directly transmitted to the Tested-Device. If the Test-Device is mounted with holders, the holders should be firmly secured to the platform of the vibration machine in such a manner as to ensure that the vibrations are directly transmitted to the holders of the Tested-Device.

  • 7.1.3 Procedures

  • 7.1.3.1 The test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 295 K ± 5 K (22 ± 5 °C);

  • 7.1.3.2 The SOC of the Tested-Device shall be adjusted in accordance with paragraph 48.5.2.

  • 7.1.3.3 All protection devices which affect the outcome of the test shall be operational.

  • 7.1.3.4. The Tested-Device shall be subjected to a vibration having a sinusoidal waveform

with a logarithmic sweep as specified in Table 3. ‘Frequency and acceleration’ between 7 Hz and 50 Hz and back to 7 Hz traversed in the vertical direction of the Tested-Device in 15 minutes. This cycle shall be repeated 12 times for a total of 3 hours.

Table 3 Frequency and acceleration 2 Frequency (Hz) Acceleration (m/s ) 7 - 18 10 18 - 30 gradually reduced from 10 to 2 30 - 50 2

  • 7.1.3.5 Notwithstanding 48.7.1.3.4, at the request of the manufacturer, a higher acceleration

level as well as a higher maximum frequency than that of the Table 3 may be used.

  • 7.1.3.6 A standard cycle of charge/discharge as described in paragraph 48.5.1 shall be

conducted.

  • 7.1.3.7 The test shall end with an observation period of 1 hour at the ambient temperature

conditions of the test environment.

  • 7.1.4 Test results

During the test, it shall be checked there is no evidence of rupture, (high-voltage), electrolyte leakage, venting, fire or explosion. The evidence of electrolyte leakage and venting shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device. The isolation resistance measured after the test shall not be less than 100 Ω/V. (high-voltage).

  • 7.2 Thermal shock

  • 7.2.1 Purpose

The purpose of this test is to verify the resistance of the REESS to sudden changes in temperature.

  • 7.2.2 Installations

This test shall be conducted either with the complete REESS or with REESS subsystem(s). If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s), the test result shall represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions. If the electronic management unit for the REESS is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells, then the electronic management unit may be omitted from installation on the Tested-Device if so requested by the manufacturer.

  • 7.2.3 Procedures

  • 7.2.3.1 The SOC of the Tested-Device shall be adjusted in accordance with paragraph 48.5.2.

  • 7.2.3.2 All protection devices which would affect the outcome of the test shall be operational.

  • 7.2.3.3 The Tested-Device shall be stored for at least 6 hours at a test temperature equal to 60

± 2 °C, followed by storage for at least 6 hours at a test temperature equal to -40 ± 2 °. This procedure shall be repeated until a minimum of 5 total cycles are completed, after which the Tested-Device shall be stored for 24 hours at an ambient temperature of 22 ± 5 °C. The maximum time interval between test temperature extremes shall be 30 minutes. However, the range of test temperature may be wider if requested by the manufacturer.

  • 7.2.3.4 The standard cycle of charge/discharge as described in paragraph 48.5.1 shall be

conducted, if not inhibited by the Tested-Device.

  • 7.2.3.5 The test shall end with an observation period of 1 hour at the ambient temperature

conditions of the test environment.

  • 7.2.4 Test results

During the test, it shall be checked if there is any evidence of rupture, (high-voltage), electrolyte leakage, venting, fire or explosion. The evidence of electrolyte leakage and venting shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device. The isolation resistance measured after the test shall not be less than 100 Ω/V. (high-voltage).

  • 7.3 Fire resistance test.

  • 7.3.1 Purpose

The purpose of this test is to verify the resistance of the REESS for securing enough time to evacuate for the occupants of the vehicle in case of fire.

  • 7.3.2 Installations

This test shall be conducted either with the complete REESS or with REESS subsystem(s). If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s), the test result shall represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions. If the electronic management unit for the REESS is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells, then the electronic management unit may be omitted from installation on the Tested-Device if so requested by the manufacturer. Where the relevant REESS subsystems are distributed throughout the vehicle, the test may be conducted on each relevant REESS subsystem.

  • 7.3.3 Procedures

  • 7.3.3.1 The test shall be conducted at a temperature of at least 273 K (0 °C);

  • 7.3.3.2 The SOC of the Tested-Device shall be adjusted in accordance with paragraph 48.5.2.

  • 7.3.3.3 All protection devices which affect the outcome of the test shall be operational.

  • 7.3.3.4 A vehicle based test or a component based test shall be performed at the discretion of

the manufacturer.

  • 7.3.3.4.1 Vehicle based test shall be according to test procedure described in paragraph

  • 7.3.3.5.

The Tested-Device shall be mounted in a testing fixture simulating actual mounting conditions as farmuch as possible; no combustible material should be used for this with the exception of material that is part of the REESS. In the case of a REESS designed for a specific vehicle use, vehicle parts which affect the course of the fire in any way shall be taken into consideration.

  • 7.3.3.4.2 Component based test shall be according to test procedure described in paragraph

  • 7.3.3.5 or 48.7.3.3.6.

In case of component based test, the manufacturer may choose either Gasoline pool fire test or LPG burner test.

  • 7.3.3.5 Gasoline pool fire test

The Tested-Device shall be placed on a grating table positioned above the fire source, for simulating actual mounting conditions as farmuch as possible. The grating table shall be constructed by steel rods, diameter 6-10 mm, with 4-6 cm in between. If needed the steel rods could be supported by flat steel parts. The flame to which the Tested-Device is exposed shall be obtained by burning commercial fuel for positive-ignition engines (hereafter called "fuel") in a pan. The quantity of fuel shall be sufficient to permit the flame, to burn for the whole test procedure. The fire shall cover the whole area of the pan (fuel tank). The pan (fuel tank) dimensions shall be chosen so as to ensure that the sides of the Tested-Device are exposed to the flame. The pan shall therefore exceed the horizontal projection of the Tested-Device by at least 20 cm, but less than 50 cm. The sidewalls of the pan (fuel tank) shall not project more than 8 cm above the level of the fuel before the test.

  • 7.3.3.5.1 The pan (fuel tank) filled with fuel shall be placed under the Tested-Device in such a

way that the distance between the level of the fuel in the pan (fuel tank) and the bottom of the Tested-Device corresponds to the design height of the Tested-Device above the road surface at the unladed mass if a vehicle based test is applied or approximately 50 cm if a component based test is applied. Either the pan (fuel tank), or the testing fixture, or both, shall be freely movable.

  • 7.3.3.5.2 During phase C (Figure 3) of the test, the pan (fuel tank) shall be covered by a

screen. The screen shall be placed 3 cm +/- 1 cm above the fuel level measured prior to the ignition of the fuel. The screen shall be made of a refractory material, as prescribed in Figure 5. There shall be no gap between the bricks and the holes in the bricks shall not be obstructed. The length and width of the frame shall be 2 cm to 4 cm smaller than the interior dimensions of the pan so that a gap of 1 cm to 2 cm exists between the frame and the wall of the pan to allow ventilation. Before the test the screen shall be the same as the ambient temperature. The firebricks may be wetted in order to guarantee repeatable test conditions.

  • 7.3.3.5.3 If the tests are carried out in the open air, sufficient wind protection shall be provided

and the wind velocity at pan level shall not exceed 2.5 km/h.

  • 7.3.3.5.4 The test shall comprise three phases B-D (Figure 2~4), if the fuel is at a temperature

of at least 293 K (20 °C). Otherwise, the test shall comprise four phases A-D.

  • 7.3.3.5.4.1 Phase A: Pre-heating (Figure 1).

The fuel in the pan shall be ignited at a distance of at least 3 m from the Tested-Device. After 60 seconds pre-heating, the pan (fuel tank) shall be placed under the Tested-Device. If the size of the

  • 7.3.3.6 LPG burner fire test set up (for component based test)

  • 7.3.3.6.1 The Tested-Device shall be placed on a test equipment, for simulating actual

mounting conditions as farmuch as possible.

  • 7.3.3.6.2 The height of the LPG burner flame shall be about 60 cm or more, without the

Tested-Device.

  • 7.3.3.6.3 The flame temperature shall be measured continuously by temperature sensors. An

average temperature shall be calculated, at least every second for the duration of the whole fire exposure, as the arithmetic average of temperatures measured by all temperature sensors fulfilling the location requirements described in paragraph 48.7.3.3.6.4.

  • 7.3.3.6.4 All temperature sensors shall be installed at a height of 5 ± 1 cm below the lowest

point of the Tested-Device's external surface. At least one temperature sensor shall be located at the centre of Tested-Device, and at least four temperature sensors shall be located within 10 cm from the edge of the Tested-Device towards its centre with nearlyas much as possible an equal distance between the sensors.

  • 7.3.3.6.5 The bottom of Tested-Device shall be exposed to the even flame directly and entirely

by fuel combustion. LPG burner flame shall exceed the horizontal projection of the Tested- Device by at least 20 cm.

  • 7.3.3.6.6 The Tested-Device shall be exposed to flame for 2 minutes after the averaged

temperature reaches 800 °C within 30 seconds. The averaged temperature shall be maintained at 800-1,100 °C for 2 minutes. , or the supply flow rate of the LPG shall be maintained at 0.32 kg/h per burner nozzle based on the GTR 20 LPG burner. Higher combustion temperatures, feed rates and longer combustion time can be applied if requested by the manufacturer.

  • 7.3.3.6.7 After direct exposure to flame the Tested-Device shall be observed until such time as

the surface temperature of the Tested-Device has decreased to ambient temperature or has been decreasing for a minimum of 3 hours.

  • 7.3.4 Test results

During the test, it shall be checked if there is any evidence of explosion on the Tested-Device.

  • 7.4 Short circuit test

  • 7.4.1 Purpose

The purpose of this test is to check the safety of REESS under the condition of external short circuit.

  • 7.4.2 Installations

This test shall be conducted either with a complete vehicle or with the complete REESS or with the REESS subsystem(s). If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s), the Tested-Device shall be able to deliver the nominal voltage of the complete REESS and the manufacturer shall demonstrate that the test result can reasonably represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions. If the electronic management unit for the REESS is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells, then the electronic management unit may be omitted from installation on the Tested-Device at the

Det. Reg. of KMVSS-MOLIT Notification No. 2021-694 MOLIT Notification 2023-7 12 Traction battery 2021.05.10 2023.01.02

©KAIDA

request of the manufacturer. For a test with a complete vehicle, the manufacturer may provide information to connect a breakout harness to a location just outside the REESS that would permit applying a short circuit to the REESS.

  • 7.4.3 Procedures

  • 7.4.3.1 The test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 293K ± 10K (20°C ± 10°C)

or at a higher temperature if requested by the manufacturer;

  • 7.4.3.2 The SOC of the Tested-Device shall be adjusted in accordance with paragraph 48.5.2.

  • 7.4.3.3 For testing with a complete REESS or REESS subsystem(s), all protection devices

which would affect the outcome of the test shall be operational;

  • 7.4.3.4 For testing with a complete vehicle, a breakout harness is connected to the

manufacturer specified location and vehicle protections systems relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational.

  • 7.4.3.5 Before the start of the test all, relevant main contactors for charging and discharging

shall be closed to represent the active driving possible mode as well as the mode to enable external charging. If this cannot be completed in a single test, then two or more tests shall be conducted. For testing with a complete REESS or REESS subsystem(s), the positive and negative terminals of the Tested-Device shall be connected to each other to produce a short circuit. The connection used for creating the short circuit (including the cabling) shall have a resistance not exceeding 5mΩ. For testing with a complete vehicle, the short circuit is applied through the breakout harness. The connection used for creating the short circuit (including the cabling) shall have a resistance not exceeding 5mΩ. The short circuit condition shall be continued until the protection function operation of the REESS terminates the short circuit current, or for at least 1 hour after the temperature measured on the casing of the Tested-Device or the REESS has stabilized, such that the temperature gradient varies by less than 4°C through 2 hours.
